messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT P1: PrivateLink/euc3 - customer connectivity degraded (DNS + asymmetric egress) – pager sent to on-call

samir: paging oncall — seeing a bunch of 5xx and DNS NXDOMAINs for customer ACME's PrivateLink endpoints in eu-central-3 (euc3). impact: app-to-database traffic + webhooks failing.

samir: quick summary from metrics: spikes at 11:02 UTC in route flaps and DNS query failures. TTLs look ok but health checks show ~30% packet loss to PL endpoints in az-c.

elaine: i can see similar from our synthetic monitors. traceroute to pl-endpoint.acme.internal stops after 3 hops inside the provider az-c fabric, then times out.

leo: @samir can you paste the pod logs and the BGP summary from the privateconnect peering?

samir: putting snippets below

```
# bgp summary from peering-edge-01
Neighbor        AS      State   Prefixes   Routes
10.200.7.2      64512   ESTAB   120        120
10.200.7.3      64512   ESTAB   118        118
10.200.7.10     64512   OPENS   0          0   <-- flapping
```

```
# curl to PL endpoint (from euc3 app)
curl -v https://pl-endpoint.acme.internal --resolve pl-endpoint.acme.internal:443:10.200.7.10
* Connected to 10.200.7.10 (10.200.7.10) port 443 (#0)
* SSL_connect timed out
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) SSL_connect timed out
```

elaine: DNS logs: multiple authoritative responses with SERVFAIL for the PrivateLink zone, followed by NXDOMAIN. Looks like recursive resolvers failing to reach the private zone which sits behind the same broken fabric.

pagerduty: @on-call samir — acknowledged. Please post status updates here.

samir: mitigation checklist: 1) confirm scope (customers affected), 2) implement temporary reroute to eu-central-2 AZ-b endpoints for affected customers, 3) escalate to infra-networking and cloud provider NOC, 4) communicate to ACME SRE. I'll start step 1 now.

leo: I can build the reroute. Proposed: add policy-based route on our egress gateway to prefer PL endpoints in euc2 for ACME prefixes, and disable propagation of the flapping path. That should reduce packet loss while they fix euc3 fabric.

kate: assigning myself to customer comms. @samir @leo keep me updated on ETA for the reroute. I'll tell ACME we have an active mitigation and will update in 15 minutes.

samir: running the policy change now. CLI below:

```
# apply PBR for ACME
netctl route add policy acme-prefixes prefer-gateway euc2-egress priority 10 match 10.60.0.0/16
netctl route disable-propagation 10.200.7.10
```

samir: applied. monitoring now.

ops-bot: Change detected: PBR applied (samir) — 3 affected sessions migrated to euc2-egress.

samir: latency for ACME back to normal within seconds. DNS still sporadic (some resolvers timing out).

leo: i'm going to force fallback for recursive resolvers to use forwarders in euc2 for acme.private. Doing that via resolver policy push.

```
# resolver policy
resolverctl push --zone acme.private --forwarders 10.30.4.2,10.30.4.3
```

elaine: dns success rate improved to ~95% after push. ACME reports fewer errors.

ops-bot: ENG-EVENT: escalated ticket to cloud-provider NOC referencing case CP-4721 (fabric flaps in euc3 az-c).

samir: provider NOC says they see intermittent fabric fabric reprogramming affecting route propagation to host 10.200.7.10 and are doing a corrective config push. They expect a 30-45m window for full stabilization.

kate: update to ACME: we routed your traffic to eu-central-2 and pushed DNS forwarders as a temporary mitigation. Provider NOC is performing a fix; estimated ETA 45m. We'll keep you posted every 15m.

leo: adding a temporary health-check-based failover for the PrivateLink VIPs so we avoid sending new sessions to the flapping instance.

samir: implemented health-check failover. New session rate to flapping host dropped to near zero. Existing sessions gracefully drained.

pagerduty: Paging summary (for postmortem): P1 - PrivateLink euc3 az-c fabric reprogramming => route propagation + DNS SERVFAIL => ACME connectivity degraded => mitigations: PBR to euc2, DNS forwarders push, health-check failover.

elainE: (typo) meant 'elaine' — will collect logs and prepare incident timeline.

ops-bot: oncall handoff scheduled: kate takes lead at 11:28 UTC for status comms; samir remains tech lead.

kate: handoff ack. next update to ACME in 14m.

samir: provider reports they completed fix at 11:40 UTC; verifying full route convergence now.

leo: bgp status now stable, previously flapping neighbor shows ESTAB; routes present.

samir: DNS resolving normally without forwarders now. rolling back resolver temporary policy.

ops-bot: mitigation rollback detected: resolver policy removed (leo).

kate: customer update: ACME confirms full service restoration, no data loss, asked for RCA and timeline. I told them we'll run a post-incident RCA and follow up within 72 hours.

pagerduty: incident marked as 'resolved' from a customer-impact perspective; keep channel open for RCA artifacts.

samir: adding initial notes to postmortem doc and assigning follow-ups: vendor confirmation on root cause, automation to detect BGP-propagation anomalies earlier, and a playbook entry for fast PBR switch to alternate AZs.

kate: thanks everyone. closing live mitigation thread.

ops-bot: Thread archived for incident 1781234567.
